title: fix(objectql, rest): RESTORE_UNIQUE_VALUE_TAKEN names an organization-scoped unique field and its label
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DU5CHkeh2msc49m4dh6kwEt)_
Fixes #32938
Area-lease pilot #33059, area A3.

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## Maintainer quick read

- **What changed:** a restore the store refuses as a unique violation now names the field when it is organization-scoped unique (`unique: 'organization'` / `true`), and every `RESTORE_UNIQUE_VALUE_TAKEN` names the field by its label (`fieldLabel`, also forwarded in the restore door's `details`).
- **Why:** the refusal asked `uniqueViolationColumn`, whose answer for the `(organization_id, FIELD)` key is no column, so the user read "(a unique value)" with no field.
- **Risk and rollback:** additive only (one new key on an existing 409 refusal; `field` now present where it was absent). Revert the one commit to roll back.
- **Look first:** `packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/restore.ts` (`uniqueValueTakenRefusal`, the `writeBack` catch), then `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (one host line), then `packages/rest/src/recycle-bin-routes.ts` (`REFUSAL_DETAIL_KEYS`).
- **Two-minute check:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run src/recycle-bin/restore.test.ts` shows 49 passed, including the new `names an organization-scoped unique field and its label` block.
- **Needed from you:** nothing; the seat lands it.

## What changes

- `restore.ts`: the store's violation at the write asks `uniqueViolationField` (the refusal's question; it sets the implied `organization_id` key part aside), not the routing question `uniqueViolationColumn`. An index name or a key of two authored columns still names no field.
- `restore.ts`: `RESTORE_UNIQUE_VALUE_TAKEN` carries `fieldLabel`, the field's display name in the restorer's locale (translation, else declared `label`), resolved by the same `displayLabels` the engine's `DuplicateRecordError` uses, and only when the field has one. The user-facing `message` names the field by it; `developerMessage` keeps the API name. Applies to the probe before the write and to the store's violation at it.
- `engine.ts`: the restore host gains `validationMessageContext` (the engine's existing locale and translator), so the label is read in the caller's locale.
- `duplicate-record-error.ts`: `displayLabels` is exported within the package (not from the package index) so both unique refusals resolve one label.
- `recycle-bin-routes.ts`: `fieldLabel` joins `REFUSAL_DETAIL_KEYS`, so the restore door forwards it in `details` beside `field`.
- Changeset: `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/rest`, `patch`.

## Tests

- `restore.test.ts`, new block (real `ObjectQL`, the file's driver double): SQLite `UNIQUE constraint failed: invoice.organization_id, invoice.invoice_no` and Postgres `23505` with `Key (organization_id, invoice_no)=...` on `detail` each refuse with `field: 'invoice_no'`, `fieldLabel: 'Invoice Number'`, the code and 409. Control on both dialects: `(organization_id, series, invoice_no)` names no `field` and no `fieldLabel`. The probe path carries the label; a `zh-CN` restorer reads the translated label; a field with no declared label carries no `fieldLabel`.
- `recycle-bin-routes.test.ts`: a `RESTORE_UNIQUE_VALUE_TAKEN` refusal forwards `field` and `fieldLabel` in `details`.

## Acceptance notes

- Premise measured on the `origin/main` source (f588614e) with the new pins: 4 failed / 45 passed (the two dialect cases, the probe label, the locale label); the controls and the no-label case passed there, as they should.
- `fieldLabel` also appears on the probe path (`field` was already named there), so one refusal code names its field the same way whichever path refused.
